ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35), as amended, together with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2011 (LI 2011/249); Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), as amended by the Companies (Disclosure of Ultimate Ownership and Control) Amendment Act 2022 and the Companies (Disclosure of Ultimate Ownership and Control) Amendment Regulations 2023; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009; and Sanctions Act 2023.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (or originating overseas company registry for foreign parent documents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only if the document originates in an Apostille Convention state: notarize if required, obtain an Apostille from the designated Competent Authority of the origin state, and lodge directly in New Zealand; do not add consular legalization. Consular legalization path only if the origin state is not an Apostille Convention state: notarize, obtain attestation from the origin state foreign ministry, then obtain legalization from the New Zealand Embassy or Consulate in the origin state; do not use an Apostille. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (for the New Zealand entity) or the relevant corporate registry of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: English-language registry certificate may be apostilled by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) or by the origin state Competent Authority if the document comes from another Convention state; direct use, no consular legalization. Consular legalization path only: MFAT authentication plus destination consular legalization for non-Convention states; never combine Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Board of Directors of the beneficial owner/parent company, notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: notary public -> Apostille from the Competent Authority of the state where the resolution is signed -> direct submission to New Zealand Companies Office, banks, or Inland Revenue; no consular legalization. Consular legalization path only: notary public -> foreign ministry authentication in the signing state -> New Zealand consular legalization in that same state; no Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholders and directors of the proposed New Zealand limited company, certified by the New Zealand registered office provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: if certified outside New Zealand, have the signatory notarized and the document apostilled by the origin Competent Authority before filing with the Companies Office; no consular legalization. Consular legalization path only: notarization, foreign ministry certification, New Zealand consular legalization in the non-Convention origin state; no Apostille. Never chain both paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing relationship bank of the beneficial owner or parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: if the bank is in a Convention state, have the bank's authorized signatory notarized and the letter apostilled by the relevant Competent Authority; accepted by New Zealand banks and IRD without consular legalization. Consular legalization path only: if the bank is in a non-Convention state, notarize the bank signatory, have the foreign ministry attest, and have the New Zealand Embassy/Consulate legalize; no Apostille in the chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/CFT UBO Declaration and Source of Wealth Affidavit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each disclosable controller and beneficial owner, executed before a notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: notarized declaration + Apostille from the origin Competent Authority of the Convention state -> direct disclosure to New Zealand Companies Office and financial institutions; no consular legalization. Consular legalization path only: notarized declaration + foreign ministry attestation + New Zealand consular legalization for non-Convention states; never add an Apostille.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, disclosable controllers, authorized signatories and beneficial owners must be screened before incorporation and on a continuing basis against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit red-flag advisories, the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN Lists, the UK and Australian consolidated sanctions lists, Interpol notices, and adverse media. The AML/CFT Act 2009 requires customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence for all PEPs, their family members and close associates, for at least 12 months after cessation of public office; source of wealth and source of funds documentation, independent legal certification, and senior partner approval are mandatory for non-FATF jurisdictions or jurisdictions without an effective AML regime. All screening matches, false-positive rationales, and decision trails must be retained in an immutable audit log and made available to the New Zealand Companies Office, IRD, and the Financial Intelligence Unit on request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Company Name Search and Reserve a Company Name online service via the New Zealand Companies Register (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must comprise Latin alphabet letters, Arabic numerals, hyphens, apostrophes and parentheses; non-Latin scripts such as Chinese characters are not accepted in the registered English name. Any foreign-language brand must be transliterated phonetically into Latin characters. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) a distinctive and unique core element; (2) a descriptive or generic qualifier; (3) a business activity or industry identifier; and (4) the mandatory legal suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. Maori words may be used without diacritics and are treated as Latin-script names.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), principally sections 12 to 20 (application, registration, certificate of incorporation and effect of registration), section 29 (default constitution), section 47 (consideration for shares), sections 83 to 91 (share register, director register and financial records), and sections 151 to 153 (appointment and qualification of directors).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, an agency of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993, filed electronically through the New Zealand Companies Office online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand imposes no minimum paid-up capital, no authorised capital concept, no statutory escrow account requirement, and no requirement to block funds in a bank account for incorporation. Shares may be issued with no par value and the directors determine the issue price and any partly paid terms in accordance with section 47 of the Companies Act 1993. Banks or immigration authorities may request evidence of available funds as substance, but the Companies Act 1993 imposes no company-law minimum.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] LIMITED (ACCOUNTING REFERENCE: ISIC 3091 MANUFACTURE OF URBAN ELECTRIC CARGO BICYCLES AND STEP-THROUGH SCOOTERS). ADOPTED by unanimous written consent of the sole incorporator and all directors on [Date] at [Time], the board having been duly constituted and in accordance with the Companies Act 1993. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT. The allotment and issue of [100] ordinary shares having no par value to the subscriber named in the shareholders register, at an aggregate subscription price of NZD [amount], is approved and ratified. The directors confirm that the consideration received for the shares is adequate and shall be recorded in the share register in accordance with section 47 of the Companies Act 1993. The board approves the share subscription agreements and authorizes the managing director to issue share certificates. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company shall be [Physical street address, city, postcode], New Zealand. The board adopts this registered office and authorizes the company secretary to file the address for service with the Registrar of Companies and to maintain the statutory records at that address. 3. BANKING AND PAYMENT AUTHORITY. The Company shall open bank accounts at [Bank name and branch], including an operating account, a payroll account, and a foreign currency account if required. [Name] and [Name] are appointed as authorized signatories; all payments exceeding NZD [amount] shall require two signatures; SWIFT, telegraphic transfers, letters of credit, and bank guarantees shall require dual approval. The board approves payment rails for SWIFT LC and TT Wire to support import of battery components and export of finished cargo bicycles. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. [Name] is appointed as Chief Executive Officer. [Name] is appointed as Company Secretary if the constitution requires one. [Name] and [Name] continue as directors. Each officer shall have authority to bind the Company in ordinary course transactions up to NZD [amount]; dispositions of assets, guarantees, borrowings over NZD [amount], and any constitution or share capital changes require board approval. 5. GOVERNANCE AND LICENSING. The board adopts the constitution tabled, or the default rules of the Companies Act 1993, and directs management to file all formation documents, apply for tax numbers, obtain all environmental and resource consents, fire safety certificates, structural approvals, and employment law registrations, and to engage legal counsel and chartered accountants as necessary. The chief executive officer is authorized to execute all documents connected with the incorporation process and to deliver certified copies of this resolution to banks, regulators, and licensed agents. CERTIFIED as a true and complete copy of the resolution adopted on [Date]. Signed by the chair of the board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation, director consent, and governance document preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office Online Services Portal at https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz/
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing the incorporation application, the practitioner shall obtain director and shareholder consent and verify all proposed officers are not disqualified under section 151 of the Companies Act 1993. Search the Companies Register for the proposed name and any conflicting marks. If the name is reserved, lodge the reservation application with the Registrar and pay the fee. Prepare the optional constitution or adopt the default rules set out in section 29 of the Companies Act 1993. Ensure the registered office address is physical, not a PO Box, and agree on a New Zealand address for service. Use the RealMe login to pre-authorise the application. Should any director consent be rejected or queried, the applicant should within 10 working days upload a witnessed affidavit of identity and disclose all prior alternate names or criminal disqualifications to the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name reservation application
Consent to appointment forms for each director and company secretary if the constitution requires one
Proof of identity for each director and shareholder, being a passport or New Zealand driver licence
Physical registered office address and New Zealand address for service
Optional constitution, or a written adoption of the Companies Act 1993 default rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects or suspends the name or consents, the incorporator shall review the register files, amend the proposed name on the same portal, obtain fresh consents using correct exact names, and resubmit with a covering explanation within 5 working days. If the objection relates to a director disqualification or tax debt, the appointor shall substitute a qualified director and file a certificate of due suitability.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation application and statutory fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, online incorporation application under the Companies Act 1993
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation application in the official portal. Attach the constitution if adopted and all consent forms. Confirm that each initial shareholder has agreed in writing to take the specified number of shares and that the minimum capital requirement is none, as New Zealand imposes no minimum paid-up capital. Declare the ISIC 3091 activity: manufacture of urban electric cargo bicycles and step-through scooters. Verify that every director is a natural person and not disqualified. Submit the certificate of compliance and pay the fee by debit or credit card. The application will be electronically verified against the New Zealand Business Number and residential address data. Ensure the statutory declarations are made on the form and that the share allocation schedule matches the consent forms. This submission is the decisive act that creates the company upon the Registrar approval.
required_dossiers: Completed electronic application for registration of a company
Constitution if adopted, signed by each director; otherwise the default rules apply
Consent to appointment forms for all first directors
Written share subscription and allocation schedule
Statutory filing fee
Director and shareholder identity documents
Registered office and address for service confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the portal raises data validation errors or the Registrar issues a defect notice, the applicant should correct the field within 10 working days. If the objection concerns the company name, the applicant must immediately reserve an alternative and amend the application. If the filing has been suspended, the same application identifier may be reactivated once all signatures have been rectified or consent forms replaced.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of incorporation and statutory register creation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, download the Certificate of Incorporation from the Companies Register. Verify that the legal entity name, unique registration number, date of incorporation, and New Zealand Business Number referenced in the certificate are identical to the approved application. Create the statutory registers required by the Companies Act 1993: register of shareholders, register of directors, and register of director interests. Put the certificate in the corporate records folder. Issue share certificates to the initial shareholder and record the issued share capital, paid-up amounts, and any no-par-value notation. Ensure that the registered office and address for service are correctly recorded and accessible. No stamp duty is payable in New Zealand on share issuance, and no notarization of the certificate is required for domestic filings, but foreign banks may require an apostille and a certified English copy.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation downloaded from the Companies Register
Initial shareholders register and share certificates
Register of directors and register of director interests
Address for service confirmation
Company minutes book and corporate records folder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical defect, file a request for correction with the Registrar attaching the certificate and a statutory declaration. If any statutory register is incomplete, obtain an internal corrective board resolution, update the register with the correct date and acquisition of shareholding, and notify the Registrar of any conflicting address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue registration, GST, employer and tax status confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department, New Zealand, myIR portal and New Zealand Business Registration process
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty days after incorporation, the company must apply to the Inland Revenue Department via the myIR portal to obtain an IRD number and to register for income tax. The New Zealand Business Number assigned at incorporation will be used. Since the company will purchase components, pay manufacturing salaries, and sell electric cargo bikes in New Zealand, the board should register for GST at the same time if the annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed NZD 60,000; otherwise register at the threshold or voluntarily to recover input tax on imports. If employees are engaged, register as an employer for PAYE, ACC and KiwiSaver. The Inland Revenue Department will issue written confirmation of tax status; that confirmation is necessary before banks finalise trade credit facilities and before customs bond arrangements can be approved.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
New Zealand Business Number
Director and shareholder identification details
Business ISIC and activity description
Expected annual turnover and import/export schedule
IR number application for company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue rejects the registration due to incomplete information, resubmit with a full schedule of foreign directors, overseas bank accounts, and anticipated cross-border transactions. If penalties are assessed for late registration, apply for administrative waiver under the Tax Administration Act 1994 on first-year compliance grounds and document any portal submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial premises consent, environmental assessment and Civil Defense licensing initiation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local territorial authority and regional council under the Resource Management Act 1991; Fire and Emergency New Zealand; WorkSafe New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm whether the intended factory location has a permitted activity status for light manufacturing under the relevant territorial authority district plan. If the assembly, painting, battery storage, or warehousing requires resource consent, prepare an Assessment of Environmental Effects addressing odour, noise, dust, hazardous substances storage, and waste disposal. Contact the regional council to determine whether an industrial discharge permit or air discharge permit is required. If the process stores hazardous substances above HSNO thresholds, apply under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996 for location and stationary container approvals. Obtain a building code compliance certificate and fire design review for factory occupancy. Apply to Fire and Emergency New Zealand for a fire evacuation scheme and to WorkSafe New Zealand for a workplace safety management system. This step is initiated only after the certificate of incorporation and is concurrent with finance.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Lease or freehold title and street address
District plan zone confirmation
Draft Assessment of Environmental Effects
Hazardous substances inventory and storage layout
Building warrant of fitness or building consent application
Fire evacuation scheme application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a resource consent is declined or notified, the applicant may submit an amended application to the council, appeal to the Environment Court on questions of fact and law within 15 working days from the decision, and adjust process design to reduce emissions. If Fire and Emergency New Zealand declines an evacuation scheme, revise the plan and provide engineered life safety systems, then reapply within 10 working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local territorial authority and regional council under the Resource Management Act 1991; Fire and Emergency New Zealand; WorkSafe New Zealand; Ministry for the Environment for national environmental policy guidance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Resource Consent for Industrial Land Use and Discharge Permit, and Hazardous Substances Location and Stationary Container Approval under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Regional Council with national policy oversight by the Ministry for the Environment, under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Assessment of Environmental Effects required if the manufacturing activity is not a permitted activity. Low-scale assembly may qualify as a permitted or controlled activity requiring only environmental registration; painting, battery handling, solvent use, wastewater discharge, and hazardous waste storage will ordinarily trigger a Full Assessment of Environmental Effects and may require limited or public notification.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Quantitative compliance thresholds are set by the relevant regional and territorial authority. Common municipal trade waste limits include pH 6.0 to 10.0, maximum temperature 38 degrees Celsius, total suspended solids not exceeding 500 mg/L, oil and grease not exceeding 100 mg/L, and no free cyanide or flammable solvent layer. Air discharge from spray booths and curing ovens must be filtered or abated so particulate matter does not exceed 10 mg/m3 and volatile organic compounds do not exceed 50 mg/m3 at stack outlet, unless a stricter site-specific resource consent limit applies. Hazardous waste storage areas must provide secondary containment of at least 110 percent of the largest storage container and comply with HSNO location and stationary container performance standards. Any discharge to land or water requires a regional council discharge permit and compliance with the National Policy Statement for Freshwater Management 2020.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety and Evacuation Scheme Approval from Fire and Emergency New Zealand, a Building Warrant of Fitness under the Building Act 2004 confirming structural fire load, fire compartmentation, means of escape and approved fire alarm systems, and a WorkSafe New Zealand workplace safety approval under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 covering hazard identification, emergency procedures, protective equipment, forklift and machinery safely, and electrical safety certification for high-voltage charging and battery assembly areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue Te Tari Taake) - New Zealand Government; secure online portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz/myir).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate NZ_LTD as a New Zealand limited company under the Companies Act 1993 through the New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), obtaining the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). Step 2: After incorporation, apply for the company's Inland Revenue Department (IRD) number using the Inland Revenue's prescribed IRD number application for a non-individual company; include the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, board resolution appointing the NZ registered office and any resident agent for service, certified identity documents for all directors and for each shareholder holding at least 25% of the shares, and tax residence certificates for offshore shareholders. Step 3: Lodge the IRD number application via myIR or in paper form to Inland Revenue; once validated, Inland Revenue issues the 8- or 9-digit IRD number which is the single tax identification number for income tax, GST, employer obligations and customs/export reconciliation. Step 4: Simultaneously assess GST registration; if the value of taxable supplies made in the course of its New Zealand taxable activity has exceeded or is likely to exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, register for GST using the GST registration module in myIR and use the quarterly GST accounting period. Step 5: For a non-resident-controlled company without a New Zealand fixed establishment, Inland Revenue may require the company to appoint an agent or resident agent for tax purposes as contemplated by the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 before the IRD number or GST registration is finalised.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a New Zealand incorporated limited company is a separate taxable entity and is subject to New Zealand corporate income tax at 28% on worldwide income if resident in New Zealand. Non-resident shareholders are not taxed on underlying company profits; distributions are instead subject to non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at applicable rates; no default pass-through treatment applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no US-style check-the-box election and no elective hybrid mismatch carve-out. A closely held NZ limited company may elect to be a Look-Through Company (LTC) under Subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, converting the entity to a flow-through basis for qualifying shareholders, provided the statutory eligibility conditions are satisfied (limited to five or fewer permitted shareholders and no corporate shareholders). This election is generally unavailable for a manufacturing company with non-resident corporate owners; the default remains entity-level taxation. The qualifying company (QC) election is closed to newly formed companies and is not available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) - New Zealand value-added tax governed by the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of gross taxable supplies in any 12-month period (GST Act 1985, s 51); registration is mandatory once the threshold is exceeded or is likely to be exceeded, and voluntary registration is available for persons carrying on a taxable activity with lower turnover. For non-resident suppliers of remote or digital services, the same NZD 60,000 remote-services registration threshold applies under s 54B.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time tax clearance, compulsory e-invoicing, API fiscal stamping or anti-fraud digital stamping regime exists in New Zealand. Tax invoices must satisfy the prescribed particulars in s 24 of the GST Act 1985, and GST returns must be filed electronically using the prescribed GST101 return form through myIR. Voluntary e-invoicing is supported on the New Zealand PEPPOL BIS 3.0 e-invoicing network, but is not mandatory. Audit and anti-fraud integrity are supported by information sharing between Inland Revenue and the New Zealand Customs Service on export entries and border movements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under s 11(1)(a) of the GST Act 1985, a supply of the electric cargo e-bikes is zero-rated if the goods are exported by the supplier as part of its taxable activity and are actually exported from New Zealand within 28 days (or any further period accepted by the Commissioner) after the time of supply. The supplier must be the exporter on the New Zealand customs export entry, the buyer must be resident outside New Zealand or otherwise outside New Zealand at the time of supply, and the goods must not have been used or consumed in New Zealand before departure. Zero-rating also applies to goods delivered to a carrier for direct shipment to an overseas destination and to certain services supplied to non-residents in connection with exported goods. The manufacturer must hold contemporaneous documentary evidence proving the movement of goods out of New Zealand to the overseas buyer; absent that evidence, the supply is taxable at 15%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service export entry (customs export declaration) lodged electronically through the Trade Single Window or approved service provider, showing the NZ manufacturer as exporter and the final foreign destination
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) evidencing physical shipment from New Zealand to the overseas buyer

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or, in New Zealand banking practice, the bank-issued foreign currency receipt/credit advice confirming repatriation of the sales proceeds from the overseas buyer to the NZ manufacturer
Commercial invoice showing the cargo e-bike description, HS classification, quantity, sale value and overseas consignee
Packing list and carrier-issued proof of delivery or final shipment certificate, supported where requested by the NZ Customs export clearance report
Internal export records showing the time of supply, actual export date, shipment terms and insurance/freight documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the zero-rating claim is not substantiated, or the export documentation is false, forged, incomplete or does not evidence physical export within the statutory period, Inland Revenue may reopen the period, reverse the zero-rating, and assess GST output tax at 15% on the full value of the supply, plus use-of-money interest. The Tax Administration Act 1994 authorises shortfall penalties up to 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims may also expose the company and responsible directors to criminal prosecution, fines and imprisonment, and retrospective clawback for all affected GST periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a pure floating exchange-rate regime with no foreign exchange controls. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) does not require approval for the remittance of dividends, repayment of shareholder loans, or liquidation proceeds to foreign residents. Non-resident shareholders may receive profit distributions and capital returns freely, subject to the Non-resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) or approved issuer levy, and subject to the entity's own AML/CFT obligations. The Overseas Investment Act 2005 applies narrowly to certain land and sensitive business assets, not to ordinary operating capital of a manufacturing subsidiary, and does not restrict daily FX flows. There is no dual exchange rate, no central bank surrender obligation, and no limitation on holding foreign currency bank accounts. The actual friction consists mainly of bank-side compliance, including source-of-funds verification, purpose-of-payment descriptions, and sanctions screening, which are required under the AML/CFT Act 2009. Consequently, treasury planning can treat New Zealand as a high-convertibility, low-friction jurisdiction for both equity and debt capital movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender requirements in New Zealand. Exporters may retain 100% of proceeds in NZD or foreign currency accounts, and no minimum conversion ratio or statutory timeline applies. Receipts must still be reflected in financial statements for tax and statistical purposes, and larger cross-border flows must be supported by documentary evidence for AML/CFT compliance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Airwallex have a limited but permissible role in the New Zealand payments landscape. They are not registered banks in New Zealand and cannot accept deposits from the public under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989; deposit-taking requires registration as a bank or licensing as a non-bank deposit taker under the Non-Bank Deposit Takers Act 2013. Offshore EMIs offering e-money accounts to New Zealand entities must comply with the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and the AML/CFT Act 2009 if they provide financial services in or into New Zealand. An offshore EMI account is not an acceptable substitute for a commercial bank account for letters of credit, capital escrow, or wholesale FX, but it can be used as an auxiliary low-value supplier payment rail. Overall feasibility rating: Medium for auxiliary payment corridors, Low as the primary treasury banking layer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand AML/CFT regulations permit remote customer verification where the bank uses robust identity verification technology, but banks retain discretion to require an interview for non-face-to-face onboarding. There is no statutory mandate that every statutory director appear physically in-branch, and remote consular proxy opening is permitted if identity documents are certified and the bank's video KYC standards are met. In practice, for a manufacturing entity with foreign shareholders, banks require at least one director or the authorised signatory to complete a live video interview; for complex ownership structures, a physical visit to an NZ branch or an approved correspondent office may be mandated. Statutory directors who are not bank signatories may not need to attend if their identity is verified via an NZ notary public or a New Zealand embassy/consulate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to identify the natural persons ultimately owning or controlling the NZ limited company due to layered nominee shareholders or discretionary trust structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarised trust deed, the full register of beneficial owners, certificates of incorporation for each owning entity, certified passport copies of all natural-person beneficial owners, a written source-of-wealth statement, a current Companies Office extract, and an organisational chart showing every shareholding layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-flow inconsistency for electric cargo e-bike manufacturing, especially procurement of batteries, motors, and power electronics from jurisdictions perceived as high-risk for smuggling or dual-use export concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit purchase orders, signed supplier contracts, packing lists, bills of lading or airway bills, marine cargo insurance certificates, commercial invoices, HS commodity codes, customs declarations, and bank payment records matching the invoice amounts and trade dates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions exposure through freight forwarders, logistics intermediaries, end customers, or distributors involved in the export and distribution of the e-bikes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a sanctions screening report covering all counterparties, end-user certificates, Incoterms, distribution agreements, restricted-party screening results, and a written compliance attestation from the designated export-control officer, supported by the company's internal sanctions policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Financing mismatch between early-stage capital injections and projected operating costs, raising concerns about round-tripping, unsecured shareholder loans, or artificial valuation of the manufacturing business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a board-approved cash flow forecast, shareholder meeting minutes, a notarised shareholder loan agreement, evidence of source of funds from verified bank accounts, an updated share register, and audited financial statements or a written confirmation from the independent accountant validating the company's financial projections.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder loan funds should be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 from the remitting bank to a New Zealand clearing bank, referencing the exact legal name of the NZ Ltd and the NZ domestic bank account number, with a clear payment description such as 'share capital injection' or 'shareholder loan'. There are no ex-ante RBNZ exchange-control approvals required, but the receiving bank will assign a balance-of-payments classification such as direct-investment equity for statistical purposes. To satisfy capital verification requirements, the company must maintain a board resolution, an updated share register, a notarised statutory declaration confirming the source and purpose of funds, and evidence of the sender's bank account. The receiving bank will perform negative screening on the sending bank, the beneficial owner, and the ultimate source of wealth before the funds are credited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements may be executed through direct SWIFT MT103 transfers for open-account supplier payments, through documentary letters of credit issued via MT700 with a set of compliant documents such as commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and certificate of origin, or through documentary collections under D/P and D/A terms using the NZ bank's correspondent banking network. For a micro-mobility OEM, letters of credit are preferred for battery and motor inventory purchases, while wire transfers are acceptable for spare parts and engineering services. The bank will require the underlying purchase order or supply contract, customs import entries, and a clear rationale for the payment amount, with continuous screening of the ultimate supplier and the receiving bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forward contracts on major currencies such as USD, EUR, AUD, GBP, and JPY, with tenors up to 36 months, subject to the NZ clearing bank's internal credit limits and RBNZ licensing standards
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies of jurisdictions with capital controls such as CNY, INR, and IDR, permitted only where the underlying import or export trade exposure can be evidenced

Cross-currency swaps between NZD and USD/EUR/JPY for tenors aligned with term debt or major capital-equipment purchases, permitted for hedging identified cash-flow risk under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2014

European-style FX options for hedging uncertain trade cash flows, permitted where the notional is supported by projected export or import exposure and the transaction is conducted with a registered commercial bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of Particulars (confirmation of company name, registered office, directors, shareholders, and constitution details)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every year on the company's assigned annual return date, which is the anniversary of incorporation; online filing opens 28 days before the due date and should be completed by the annual return date itself.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the due date constitutes an offence under the Companies Act 1993; directors may be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding NZD 10,000. The Registrar may also issue a Notice of Intention to Remove the company from the Register after persistent non-filing, and removal leads to dissolution, cessation of trading capacity, and vesting of the company's remaining assets in the Crown. Reinstatement after removal requires a court or Registrar restoration process and payment of prescribed restoration fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: General Purpose Financial Report (GPFR) and independent auditor's report, when the company meets medium or large size thresholds under the Financial Reporting Act 2013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (filing); External Reporting Board (accounting and auditing standards)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements must be completed and approved by the board within 5 months after balance date; for a standard 31 March balance date, practical completion is required no later than 31 August, and the statements are filed with the Companies Office as part of the company's annual return delivery cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Companies Act 1993; each director may be liable to fines for failure to prepare, audit, or file financial statements. Persistent non-delivery is also a ground for Registrar strike-off. Deliberately false or misleading statements can attract higher criminal penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company income tax return (IRD IR4) and terminal tax payment, including any relevant tax losses and international disclosure schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (IRD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return is due and terminal tax must be paid by 7 July following the balance date; for a non-standard balance date, the due date is the 7th day of the fourth month after balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: IRD applies late filing penalties for an overdue IR4, initially NZD 50 and escalating for repeated or prolonged non-filing. Late payment penalties include an immediate 1% penalty, a further 4% penalty after 7 days, and an additional 1% per month on the unpaid amount. IRD use-of-money interest applies annually on outstanding tax. Serious persistent non-compliance can lead to IRD enforcement, debt collection, and personal liability for directors in certain cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST return and GST payment, where the company is registered for New Zealand goods and services tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (IRD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: GST returns are due one month after the end of the taxable period. For a standard two-monthly GST period ending 31 March, the return is due by 28 April; for monthly filers, the return is due by the 28th day of the following calendar month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid GST attracts an immediate 1% late payment penalty, a further 4% penalty after 7 days, and a continuing 1% per month thereafter. Late filing of GST returns triggers late filing penalties and may expose directors or the company to IRD compliance and enforcement action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer annual schedule and year-end reconciliation (IR348), PAYE/ESCT finalization, and annual Fringe Benefit Tax return where the company employs staff or provides fringe benefits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (IRD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Employer schedules and deductions are reported by the 20th of the following month for paper filing or within 2 working days after each payday for electronic filing; the employer annual schedule is due by 20 July following a 31 March balance date; the annual FBT return is due and paid by 20 July following the FBT year ending 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late employer and FBT returns incur NZD 50 late filing penalties per return, escalating for repeated and prolonged failures. PAYE and FBT unpaid by due date incur initial 1%, additional 4% after 7 days, and 1% per month penalties. Inland Revenue may directly pursue directors and officers for unpaid PAYE deductions because those deductions are held in trust.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit is mandatory for a New Zealand company that is medium or large under the Financial Reporting Act 2013. A company is medium when it is not large and, at balance date, total assets exceed NZD 10 million, total turnover exceeds NZD 5 million, or it has 50 or more employees. A company is large when, at balance date, total assets exceed NZD 60 million, total turnover exceeds NZD 30 million, or it has 80 or more employees. The audit must be performed by a person qualified as a New Zealand auditor under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, who must express an opinion in accordance with ISA (NZ) standards. Small companies are exempt from statutory audit unless the company's constitution or shareholders require one, the company is an FMC reporting entity or issuer, or the audit is otherwise required by a bank, lender, or contractual covenant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with New Zealand generally accepted accounting practice (NZ GAAP) established by the External Reporting Board (XRB). For-profit entities use New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS) for Tier 1, NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosures (RDR) for Tier 2, and simplified or simple format reporting standards for eligible Tier 3 and Tier 4 private entities. The legal framework is the Companies Act 1993, Financial Reporting Act 2013, and the External Reporting Board's accounting standards for for-profit entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not operate a separate annual UBO filing system for ordinary private limited companies. Beneficial ownership is evidenced through the company's own share register, director registers, and the Companies Office public register. The annual return must confirm current shareholders and directors, and any share transfer or allotment must be recorded in the share register without unreasonable delay, in practice within 10 working days. Changes of directors, registered office, or address for service must be notified to the Companies Office within 10 working days. If a shareholding transfer crosses an overseas-investment control threshold, the transaction may separately require approval or notification under the Overseas Investment Act. There is no 30-day shareholding-reporting window in New Zealand other than the next annual return cycle; the 10-working-day corporate register update rule governs.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Records of share allotments and transfers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 to USD 18,000 per year where a statutory audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% flat corporate income tax rate (Income Tax Act 2007, Schedule 1, Part A, clause 1; no sub-national corporate income tax in New Zealand's unitary fiscal system)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory corporate tax holidays, no patent box, and no export zones exist in New Zealand. Principal incentives: (i) Research and Development Tax Incentive under Part LZ -- a refundable credit equal to 15% of eligible R&D expenditure (min NZD 50,000 per income year, max NZD 120 million per group), with elective 3-year admission for start-ups; (ii) immediate deduction (low-value asset write-off) for depreciable assets under NZD 5,000, and 100% immediate deduction for qualifying commercial buildings, residential fit-out, and asset categories specified under Schedule 20; (iii) depreciation loading has been abolished; (iv) imputation credit system ensures distributed profit is not doubly taxed at resident-shareholder level, which is a structural rate-reduction feature for inbound investors using New Zealand holding stacks.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carry-forward with no statutory time cap (s IA 4 Income Tax Act 2007); utilisation is conditional on continuity of beneficial ownership of 49% or more (s IA 5) or the same-or-similar-business test (s IA 6) after an ownership breach; no loss carry-back is currently available (the temporary COVID-19 one-year carry-back expired for the 2022 and later income years).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) and, where applicable, the IR4J (companion schedule for tax adjustments) and Schedule 8 (International Related Party Disclosure); mandatory electronic filing through the Inland Revenue Department's 'myIR' online portal or direct-to-IRD software (e.g., Xero, MYOB, CCH); paper filing is available only on explicit IRD dispensation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return (once per income year). The same income year carries three provisional tax instalments for taxpayers with residual income tax above NZD 5,000 (standard uplift method: instalments generally due 28 August, 15 January and 7 May for a 31 March balance date) -- an interim quarterly settlement rhythm that binds cash flow even though the return itself is annual.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed on or before 7 July immediately following the balance date (i.e., within about 3 months after year-end). For a substituted non-standard balance date, the due date is the 7th day of the month that falls six months after the balance date (e.g., a 30 September balance date is due 7 April). Terminal tax (the residual balance above provisional tax) is due 7 April for a 31 March balance date (or the 7th day of the month falling 12 months after the balance date), but the return filing obligation is the earlier 7 July date. Registered tax agents can obtain an extension of the filing date to the 31st day of the month following the original due date (and further extensions for the agent's portfolio in some circumstances); the statutory terminal tax date is not extended.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identifier block: IRD number, legal name, balance date, CFC details, and imputation company status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the New Zealand IRD number and the exact legal name shown on the Companies Office registration. Non-resident-owned NZ Ltd must disclose the percentage of foreign ownership and the ultimate controlling jurisdiction in the supplementary disclosure block; use the jurisdiction code list issued in the IR4 Guide.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income: gross accounting income in NZD including gross sales of electric cargo e-bikes, spare parts, commissions, foreign currency gains on trade receivables, and taxable financial arrangement income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all income derived from New Zealand sources and, subject to CFC rules, all income derived by the NZ resident company worldwide. Convert overseas sales into NZD at the prevailing IRD conversion rate (spot rate or IRD's published quarterly exchange rates); do not net off export freight or customs duties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses: deductible expenditure and losses incurred in deriving assessable income under s DA 1 (materials, direct labour, manufacturing overheads, R&D consumables, royalties, freight, warranty provisions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deduct expenses supported by contemporaneous documentation. Recharge allocations from an offshore parent (e.g., head-office management fees, global IT charges, intercompany royalties or licence fees for e-bike drive-train IP) must satisfy the arm's length principle and New Zealand's transfer pricing record-keeping rules; non-compliant recharges are denied and attract shortfall penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit/(loss) per statutory financial statements, reconciled to the NZ GAAP (XRB A1) accounting profit for the income year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the statutory financial statements in English. If the non-resident parent group reports under IFRS in USD, attach a reconciliation of the NZ entity's standalone IFRS financial statements to tax values, adjusting for FX translation differences and cross-border intercompany balances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back adjustments: non-deductible expenditure such as 50% of entertainment, non-deductible penalties and fines, depreciation on non-qualifying assets, and interest on tax shortfall.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any intercompany interest expense in excess of the arm's length limited by the New Zealand thin-capitalisation ratio (60% of assets for non-resident-owned groups) and the 'restricted transfer pricing' rules for internal debt (sections FE 12 and GC 15). Also add back withholding tax penalties and any foreign exchange losses on non-trade shareholder loans.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible adjustments: tax depreciation (diminishing value or straight-line under Schedule 17), annual amortisation of intellectual property, R&D expenses subject to the 15% credit, and low-value asset write-offs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only deductions that present no double-dip: a non-resident parent cannot claim depreciation on goods that are the subject of an intra-group secondment, and any related-party lease or licence fee must be at arm's length. Allocation of R&D credit amounts between New Zealand and foreign-registered IP must be consistent with the country of first charge and legal ownership chain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income/(loss) for the year; loss carry-forward from prior years applied against current-year net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the 49% shareholder continuity test before applying losses: if the non-resident shareholding changed by more than 51% during the year, prior losses are extinguished unless the same-or-similar-business exception is met. Losses cannot be offset intra-group on a consolidated basis in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income and the 28% tax calculation on that taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the flat 28% company rate; there is no progressive company schedule. Compute tax on internet gateways and e-bike subscription leases under the financial arrangement rules where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and rebates: the R&D tax credit (15% of eligible expenditure), foreign tax credits for overseas branch income, and the transitional imputation credit rebate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The R&D credit is claimed via supplementary schedule IR4S (R&D tax incentive); attach IRD approval of the R&D project plan if the credit exceeds NZD 2 million. A non-resident-owned entity with R&D conducted by a New Zealand subsidiary should ensure the subsidiary owns or licenses the IP at arm's length; otherwise, the credit is denied and the evasion/incentive fraud provisions apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit memorandum block: resident withholding tax on interest/dividends received, PAYE tax credits, provisional tax paid, and credits for the Research and Development Tax Incentive.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that every related-party lending transaction is supported by an IRD withholding tax certification (IR 291/AIL or an exemption certificate). Provide the foreign tax credit breakdown in the accompanying international schedule if foreign tax is claimed under a DTA or under the Foreign Tax Credit regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax (RIT) due or refund: the amount due after all credits, being the basis for provisional tax, terminal tax, late payment penalties, and Use-of-Money Interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Residual income tax above NZD 5,000 triggers provisional tax obligations; NRWT already withheld on outbound dividends or royalties is not a credit available to the company. Ensure that terminal tax is paid in full by the statutory terminal date -- an unpaid terminal tax balance is now collected through IRD debt collection, including departure prohibition orders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compulsory declaration of cross-border related-party transactions: aggregate values of intercompany sales, purchases, loans, interest, royalties, management fees, and the taxpayer's transfer pricing position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration must quantify, by jurisdiction of the related party, transactions with related parties. Completing the schedule on a best-effort basis is insufficient: Inland Revenue cross-checks disclosed values against the taxpayer's Local File and Master File. Where the total value equals or exceeds NZD 10 million, attach the Local File; where NZD 100 million, attach the Master File; and where the group's consolidated revenue is NZD 1.1 billion or more, confirm automatic exchange of Country-by-Country information.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty (LFP): NZD 250 for a company with annual gross income under NZD 2 million and NZD 500 for gross income over NZD 2 million, imposed immediately upon the filing default; a further equal penalty is imposed if the return is still outstanding 30 days after the original due date. Inland Revenue may in addition issue a default-assessment on information held and impose a 'failure to provide a return' absolute-liability fine of up to NZD 25,000 under s 143 TAA 1994. Unpaid tax accrues a late payment penalty of 1% on the day after the due date, an additional 4% after a further 7 days, and a further 1% for each additional month of default, together with daily Use-of-Money Interest at the prescribed underpayment rate (set quarterly; approximately 8.3%-9.2% during 2025). Criminal prosecution may be added where the failure is part of a pattern of evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) under Part RJ, Income Tax Act 2007 on dividends paid by a New Zealand company to a non-resident shareholder, whether the dividend is cash, a property dividend, or an imputed credit. There is no resident-shareholder withholding because the imputation system attaches 28% imputation credits. Treaty-reduced rates generally apply: 15% for portfolio shareholdings and 5% for holdings of 10% or more of the voting power (e.g., under the Australia, United States, United Kingdom, Singapore, China, Japan, Korea and the conventional OECD-pattern DTAs). A New Zealand 'Supplementary Dividend' mechanism may be elected to carry the treaty rate on dividends with imputation credits, where the supplementary dividend is itself fully taxed at 33% for the resident shareholder but deductible at the company level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain the treaty rate, the payer must hold, before the payment date, (i) a current Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the recipient's residence jurisdiction, (ii) a completed NRWT Treaty Claim Declaration (IR 290 or the IRD treaty claim schedule) confirming that the recipient is the beneficial owner, has no New Zealand permanent establishment to which the dividend/interest/royalty is attributable, and satisfies any Limitation-of-Benefits or Principal Purpose Test under the applicable DTA and the OECD MLI, and (iii) where relevant, evidence of a 10% voting-power threshold for the 5% dividend rate, and an ownership/control structure certificate for interest paid to an associated lender. Inland Revenue permits retrospective treaty relief claims, but the reduced rate is not available unless the payer has applied the correct rate; any excess withheld must be reclaimed by the non-resident by filing a New Zealand tax return and adducing the TRC, a process that routinely takes 6-18 months with IRD review. For interest, the borrower may elect to pay the 2% Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) in lieu of NRWT only where the lender is an unassociated person and the debenture is a registered public issue (or the lender is an associated non-resident exemption case under s 86J(3)); AIL election is irrevocable, changes the lender's gross-up economics, and requires borrower registration with IRD.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory NRWT 15% on royalty payments (including licensed patents, designs, trade marks, know-how, and software royalties); treaty rates commonly 5% (United States, Singapore, Australia) or 10% (United Kingdom, China, Japan, Korea, Germany) and 15% in the absence of a treaty or where the recipient is not the beneficial owner. Interest: statutory NRWT 15%; treaty rate typically 10% under United States, Australia, UK, China, Japan, Korea and Singapore DTAs; a nil or reduced rate is available for government-to-government lending and approved infrastructure bonds; the 2% Approved Issuer Levy can substitute for the 15% statutory rate on qualifying public-issued debentures with unassociated lenders. Non-arm's-length or thinly-capitalised interest is recharacterised and denied deductibility, per sections GC 14-GC 16, and the payments are then treated as a deemed dividend subject to 15%-30% NRWT with attendant penalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory where the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions equals or exceeds NZD 10 million in the income year. Master File: mandatory where the aggregate value equals or exceeds NZD 100 million in the income year. Country-by-Country Report: mandatory notification (and filing by the ultimate parent or the tax resident surrogate) where the multinational group's consolidated turnover equals or exceeds NZD 1.1 billion. Small-sized taxpayers with related-party transactions below NZD 1 million for a financial year with a total worldwide turnover under NZD 60 million are not subject to the contemporaneous documentation retention requirements, but they remain subject to transfer pricing adjustments and can be asked to produce documentation on audit. All thresholds are computed in New Zealand dollars (NZD); the documentation must be prepared in English, updated to the end of the income year, and retained for seven years.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP) Method -- preferred for commodities and arm's-length benchmark of e-bike and component sales with third-party distributors or OEM customers
Resale Price Method -- applied to distribution affiliates where goods are resold to independent customers and where the reseller contributes no substantial value-add
Cost Plus Method -- applied to contract manufacturing, assembly, and intra-group shared R&D or engineering services provided by the New Zealand entity to the non-resident group

Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) -- the most frequently accepted and practical method for mid-market and OEM structures, using full-cost or operating-expense-based profit level indicators (e.g., Berry ratio for limited-risk distributors)
Transactional Profit Split Method -- applied to the integrated development, licensing or manufacturing of the e-bike IP, where both sides make unique and valuable contributions and share synergies
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a code of Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the mould of the United Arab Emirates or Caribbean jurisdictions, and there is no statutory minimum number of employees or physical premises. Substance is nevertheless required as a matter of tax law and anti-avoidance doctrine through six enforcement mechanisms: (i) statutory residency -- a company incorporated in New Zealand is a New Zealand tax resident (s YD 2, ITA 2007), so it cannot renounce residence by management-and-control movement without an approved migration and continuity ruling; (ii) the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s BG 1) and the associated 'tax avoidance arrangement' reconstruction powers, under which an arrangement with no real commercial substance is void as against the Commissioner and recharacterised at full fair value with a shortfall penalty of 100% of the resulting tax shortfall; (iii) the BEPS-compliant transfer pricing regime (ss GC 13-GC 16) requiring the commercially rational allocation of profit relative to the actual business functions, assets contributed, and risks assumed by the New Zealand manufacturing entity; (iv) the thin-capitalisation regime (Part FE) applying to non-resident closely-held groups, restricting related-party debt to 60% debt-to-assets and prescribing a 'restricted transfer pricing' (deemed credit rating) approach to internal borrowings so that artificially loaded debt is economically neutralised; (v) the MLI Principal Purpose Test limiting treaty access where obtaining treaty benefit was one of the principal purposes of the structure; and (vi) the High-Value Dealer obligations under the AML/CFT Act for cash-intensive dealing, which, while not a tax substance rule, creates an independent record-keeping and beneficial-ownership verification requirement that the tax audit may discover. An NZ Ltd engaged in genuine manufacturing of urban electric cargo e-bikes -- with a staffed production facility, substantive assembly operations, quality control, warranty servicing, R&D personnel and risk-bearing revenue -- will readily satisfy any substance challenge; conversely, a letterbox holding company without operations will fail, and the IRD will reattribute profit, deny treaty benefits and impose penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent False Tax Returns (TAA 1994, ss 143A, 143B)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing an IR4 that omits gross proceeds from e-bike sales, overstates deductible expenses, creates fictitious R&D expenditure to claim the 15% R&D tax credit, or uses altered or backdated intercompany agreements to manufacture an arm's-length defence. Also includes the deliberate recycling of cash through related-party 'consulting' payments without services being rendered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Conviction under s 143B: imprisonment for up to 5 years and/or a fine of up to NZD 50,000 per offence for any person; a body corporate is liable to fines of up to NZD 250,000; the Commissioner also imposes a civil shortfall penalty of 150% of the evaded tax, and the limitation period for reassessment is extended indefinitely. In practice, the IRD conducts criminal referral to the Serious Fraud Office for falsification of books, and assets obtained from the offence are subject to restraint and forfeiture under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause the false return are personally exposed to prosecution as principals or parties to the evasion (aiding, abetting, counselling or procuring), with imprisonment up to 5 years and personal fines; on conviction a director is disqualified from managing a company for up to 5 years under s 383 Companies Act 1993. Inland Revenue may issue a Departure Prohibition Order under s 158 TAA restraining such a director from leaving New Zealand until all assessed tax, penalties and interest are paid, and the director will be jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall where the liability was incurred by reckless trading within the meaning of s 135 Companies Act 1993.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Tax Avoidance and Abusive Tax Positions (GAAR, s BG 1 ITA 2007)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Arranging the ownership and intercompany flow so that the New Zealand entity is structured as a mere contract manufacturer capturing a Berry-ratio or low single-digit margin, while the non-resident related distributor, IP owner, or financing affiliate captures the residual profit, or routing royalty payments through an intermediary jurisdiction lacking substantive R&D or licensing functions; concluding intercompany agreements that do not reflect actual conduct (e.g., a written agent agreement where the NZ entity actually bears inventory risk and accepts purchase orders).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The arrangement is void as against the Commissioner; the IRD reconstructs the transaction at arm's-length consideration (including substituting a notional arm's-length interest rate on related-party debt), disallowance of deductions, and the shortfall penalty for an abusive tax position (100% of the tax shortfall) or, for an unacceptable tax position, 20%; interest and late payment penalties accrue from the original due date. The time bar that otherwise limits reassessment to four years does not apply to avoidance arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who designed or authorised the arrangement can be assessed personally for the company's tax shortfall in the context of insolvency under s 300 Companies Act 1993 (liability for reckless trading), and the IRD will name them in civil proceedings and seek contribution; criminal liability for 'evasion' arises where the arrangement is accompanied by concealment or false documentation. An interdiction order may be lodged against company assets to prevent profit-stripping distributions during the investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Off-Market Intercompany Pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare, update and retain the contemporaneous Local File and Master File once cross-border related-party transactions equal or exceed NZD 10 million and NZD 100 million respectively; failing to disclose related-party transactions in Schedule 8 of the IR4; pricing the intercompany sale of electric cargo e-bikes at a margin below the OECD arm's-length range without adjustment; or applying an unsupported profit split to arrive at losses in New Zealand while the group is consistently profitable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue adjusts taxable income using the arm's-length principle under s GC 13; the taxpayer is denied deduction for unpaid offshore interest (s GC 14); the thin-capitalisation rules limit interest to a 60% debt-to-asset ratio or the worldwide group ratio and recharacterise excess interest as a dividend; shortfall penalties apply at 20% (unacceptable tax position), 40% (gross carelessness), or 100% (abusive tax position) of the reconstructed tax shortfall. Documentation is also a condition for mitigation: ILT/IRD practice requires that documentation be prepared before the tax return is filed to qualify for penalty relief on a 'reasonable care' defence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign a return knowing that the transfer pricing position is unsupportable are personally exposed to the evasion offence; in a liquidation, the Commissioner can seek a personal liability order for the company's tax debt against directors who failed to maintain tax records or who allowed the company to trade while insolvent (s 135-136 Companies Act 1993), and may proceed against the directors' assets through civil proceedings. A travel ban remains available for unpaid assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Profit Repatriation Without Withholding / Mischaracterised Dividends and Interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, royalty or interest to a non-resident parent or affiliate without withholding NRWT at the 30% (dividend) or 15% (interest/royalty) statutory rate, mislabelling a dividend as a principal repayment on a sham loan, or extracting New Zealand funds through a management-fee recharge or IP assignment with no arm's-length consideration; structuring the e-bike brand IP to be owned by a related Singapore or Hong Kong entity solely to shift goodwill and royalty yield offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withheld NRWT not deducted is recovered from the payer, together with penalties equal to 100% of the unreported amount in aggravated cases; the payment is recharacterised as a dividend or royalty subject to gross-up; the interest deduction is denied; and use-of-money interest and late payment penalties are added. If the arrangement involved sham documentation, the directors face criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorised the payment knowing it was a taxable distribution become personally liable for the company's withholding obligation to the extent the company is unable to pay, and are jointly liable for any penalties; the departure prohibition order can be used as a collection tool, and criminal dishonesty charges can be pursued under the Crimes Act 1961 for obtaining a pecuniary advantage by deception.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Structure, Poor Beneficial-Ownership Transparency and MLI/PPT Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an NZ Ltd with no directors' meetings, tax invoices, employees or premises while booking dividend or royalty income and claiming treaty relief from the United States, Australia or Singapore; failing to file the company register's new beneficial-ownership declaration under the Companies Act 1993 (for NZ company ownership disclosure effective April 2025); or using Irish or Delaware holding-company layers without a business purpose other than accessing the Australia/NZ/Australia DTA's 5% dividend rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test, treaty benefits are denied and the 30% NRWT is restored; the GAAR voids the arrangement; shortfall penalties at the 100% 'abusive tax position' level apply; the company is subject to strike-off by the Registrar of Companies under s 318 Companies Act 1993; and the anti-money-laundering reporting obligation for beneficial owners exposes the structure to AML/CFT penalties of up to NZD 2 million for a body corporate for non-reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director of a shell company who is a party to the sham may be personally liable for the tax shortfall under the universal anti-avoidance jurisprudence, banned from managing companies for up to 5 years, and restrained from travel under departure prohibition orders; where funds were laundered through the shell, the director faces money-laundering offences under s 243 Crimes Act 1961 carrying a maximum of 7 years' imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT High-Value Dealer and Cash Transaction Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a high-value dealer by accepting at least NZD 10,000 in cash (or bearer negotiable instruments) in a single transaction for the supply of electric cargo bikes or fleet units, without conducting customer due diligence, beneficial-ownership verification, post-transaction reporting, and ongoing monitoring; failing to report a suspicious transaction involving the laundering of the proceeds of tax evasion through trade mispricing; or structuring cash receipts into instalments below NZD 10,000 specifically to avoid the AML regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, non-compliance with a regulation attracts civil penalty up to NZD 200,000 for a natural person and NZD 2 million for a body corporate; for reckless or deliberate contravention of a fundamental obligation, penalties are up to NZD 400,000 / NZD 4 million, and criminal liability of up to 2 years' imprisonment and NZD 300,000 fines applies; the Department of Internal Affairs may also censure and require independent audit of the compliance programme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers are individually liable for a failure to supervise or a deliberate breach; the Court can make banning orders disqualifying them from acting as a director for a period the Court fixes; the underlying criminal proceeds can be restrained under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009, and the AML regulator routinely refers tax evasion and money-laundering cases to the Financial Intelligence Unit and the Serious Fraud Office, resulting in travel-banned status and confiscation of personal assets.
